items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin.

ctx.x: I just want to get back a little so we won't digress too far, Danny. When you were a kid around New Orleans, when did you first start to think about getting into music?

Well, I didn't think about it too much. I was going to school. And I'm hearing this music all the time, and I'd see these musicians, they're celebrated. I've got four uncles -- Paul Barbarin, Louis Barbarin, Lucien Barbarin, Willie Barbarin. We live in the neighborhood, in the Seventh Ward, where there's quite a few halls -- the (?) Hall, the Jean Ami Hall, the Franz(?) Ami Hall, the New Hall. And on Ledgerfield Avenue there was about four or five White halls. And there was music all the time. And I'm listening…

And my uncles... My grandfather being in the brass band, he played the funerals with the Onward Brass Band, which was the greatest brass band at that time. And there was a rivalry between Manny Perez and George Moret(?), who was the leader of the Excelsior Band. And I'm hearing this. And my uncles, they're talkin' about who's who and who ain't. And it's a celebrate thing, and everybody is celebrated. So they would talk who could play and who couldn't, and who rated... Like most people, the kids in town, they…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So that wasn’t nothing new to me, because I had these two great drummers, my two uncles.

ctx.x: Beating. Yeah, they’d be beating. Paul [Barbarin], he was the oldest. Paul would be beating. He was doing . . . After I joined Cab Calloway’s band, and Cozy Cole would stay in the dressing room all day, practicing ratamacues, flamamadiddles, flama­ ramadiddles, all them kind of drum movements, and I’d look at him. Everybody [? (inaudible)]. I heard my uncle. I had four uncles. All of them played drums. They was doing that [expletive deleted]. But doing it with a feeling, not just a military thing like Cozy was…
Did Lucien . . . Louis and Paul were very famous and well-known. Did Lucien ever record or did he stay in New Orleans?

items.title: Louis Barbarin Interview, 1960-06-22
items.q: In 1947, I went to New York with Danny Barker, speculating on his job.

ctx.x: I learned drums by playing on my mother's chairs, the two forks. That was in the year of 1916. My father bought my brother, Paul, a set of drums. And Paul was playing around here with different bands. And he was called to Chicago to play with Manuel Ferrer's band at the Royal Garden in Chicago. My first set of drums was the one Paul was working with in Chicago. And he sent them to me because he bought some new ones. Well, I was on the way to start playing the first job. I played a house party, just a piano and…
I don't believe you gave us your birth date exactly. And just what part of the city you were born in. I didn't want that. Right at the very beginning. Okay. I was born in New Orleans.
